content: The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends that individuals with diabetes, along with their caregivers and family members, should be screened for signs of diabetes distress at least once every year. This screening should occur more frequently in situations where diabetes management targets are not being achieved or during times of significant life transitions. Elevated levels of diabetes distress have been linked to worse diabetes-related outcomes, including reduced adherence to self-care behaviors and increased hemoglobin A1C levels.
